title: The Coonoor Emeralds
subtitle: Coonoor Railway Station, Nilgiris — 3 December 1947
intro: Four months after Independence, the Maharani of Kumarapuram is sending her famous emerald necklace up the Nilgiri Mountain Railway to Ooty for a wedding.
Overnight, the jewels sat locked in the Station Master's safe at Coonoor. At 7:00 AM, when the safe was opened for the toy train, the seal was intact — and the necklace was fake. Paste and glass.
Three people had business near that safe this morning. The train leaves at 8:00. Find the thief before it does.

briefing.victim: The Maharani of Kumarapuram's emerald necklace (valued at Rs. 2 lakh)
briefing.found: Replaced with a paste replica, discovered at 7:00 AM
briefing.notes: The safe has one key, held by the Station Master. The case seal was unbroken.

props.name: Pot-bellied Stove
props.examine: A coal stove, ticking with heat. A coal scuttle beside it, freshly filled.

props.name: Station Clock
props.examine: Railway time: 7:14 AM. The 8:00 to Ootacamund is chalked on the board beside it.

props.name: Luggage Trunk
props.examine: A steamer trunk stencilled 'D. CLARKE — MADRAS'. Locked.

props.name: Safe
props.examine: A Chubb safe, door open. One key — the Station Master's. The jewel case inside still wears its unbroken wax seal.

props.name: Railway Map
props.examine: The Nilgiri Mountain Railway: Mettupalayam, Kallar, Coonoor, Wellington, Lovedale, Ootacamund. Rack and pinion, all the way up.

clues.name: The Paste Necklace
clues.description: A clever fake — green glass in a gilt setting. But on the inside of the clasp, scratched almost too small to see: 'M.P.W.' The mark of the Madras Paste Works.

clues.name: Station Log Book
clues.description: '6:30 AM — Safe opened at request of Mr. D. Clarke, insurance assessor, to inspect the Kumarapuram jewels. Inspection 10 mins. Case re-sealed by Mr. Clarke with his own wax.' Nobody else opened the safe all night.

clues.name: Torn Receipt
clues.description: Fished from the dustbin, torn in four: 'MADRAS PASTE WORKS, Mount Road. One replica necklace, emerald pattern, to customer's drawing. Paid in full — D.C.'

clues.name: Pawn Ticket
clues.description: A Coonoor pawnbroker's ticket for 'two gold bangles', in the name R. D'Souza, dated last week. Someone needed money.

clues.name: Coal-dusted Boots
clues.description: A porter's boots by the stove, black with coal dust right up to the laces. Whoever wore them spent the early morning hauling coal on the platform, not in an office.

suspects.name: Desmond Clarke
suspects.bio: 45. Assessor for the Bombay & Madras Insurance Co. Travels with a jeweller's loupe and a very large trunk.
suspects.greeting: Desmond Clarke, Bombay & Madras Insurance. Dreadful business. My company will want this solved before that train leaves, Detective — and so do I.

dialogue.ask: When did you last see the real necklace?
dialogue.answer: Last night at the palace, when it was packed. Genuine, every stone. I swear it.
dialogue.statement: Clarke claims he last saw the real necklace at the palace last night.

dialogue.ask: The log says you opened the safe at 6:30 this morning.
dialogue.answer: Ah — yes. Routine inspection. I'd quite forgotten. The stones looked perfectly fine to me then. Perfectly.
dialogue.statement: Clarke admits he inspected the jewels alone at 6:30 AM and re-sealed the case.

dialogue.ask: Madras Paste Works. Paid in full, 'D.C.'
dialogue.answer: Plenty of men in Madras have the initials D.C., Detective. I— I'd like to sit down.
dialogue.statement: Clarke goes pale at the paste-works receipt.

suspects.name: Rosalind D'Souza
suspects.bio: 27. From Mangalore. Escorting the necklace to Ooty. Her family is in debt.
suspects.greeting: Rosalind D'Souza. The Maharani trusted me with those emeralds. If they're not found, Detective, I'm finished.

dialogue.answer: Here in the waiting room, from six. Mr. Clarke went into the office alone at half past — he said insurance rules required it.
dialogue.statement: Rosalind says Clarke went into the office alone at 6:30 AM.

dialogue.ask: Why did you pawn your bangles?
dialogue.answer: My father's doctor's bills. It's shameful, not criminal. If I'd stolen two lakh of emeralds, would I need to pawn my mother's bangles?
dialogue.statement: Rosalind pawned her bangles for her father's medical bills.

suspects.name: Murugan
suspects.bio: 40. Porter at Coonoor for fifteen years. Wears the red railway coat.
suspects.greeting: Vanakkam, sir. Murugan, porter. Fifteen years on this platform — never one paisa missing.

dialogue.ask: Where were you between six and seven?
dialogue.answer: On the platform, sir, loading coal for the engine. Look at my boots! Station Master sahib can tell you.
dialogue.statement: Murugan says he was loading coal on the platform from 6 to 7 AM.

dialogue.ask: Did you see anyone near the office?
dialogue.answer: Only the insurance sahib, sir. He came out at twenty to seven, wiping his hands with a handkerchief. In this cold, he was sweating.
dialogue.statement: Murugan saw Clarke leave the office at 6:40, sweating in the cold.

timeline.text: The jewel case is sealed and locked in the Station Master's safe.
Murugan begins loading coal on the platform.
Mr. Clarke has the safe opened and inspects the jewels alone.
Clarke leaves the office, sweating in the cold.
The safe is opened for the train. The necklace is paste.

motives.text: Greed — swap the real stones for a pre-made fake and sell them
To pay a family's medical debts

explanation: Desmond Clarke stole the Kumarapuram emeralds.

Weeks ago he commissioned a replica from the Madras Paste Works, drawn from the insurance photographs. At 6:30 AM he used his authority as assessor to have the safe opened, swapped the real necklace for the fake during his 'inspection', and re-sealed the case with his own wax.
The real emeralds are in the false bottom of his trunk. He threw away the receipt — but not far enough.
